financial_health.basis: Stated in the earnings release. Any link to debt is not stated and is not assumed.
financial_health.claim: The company acknowledged ongoing discussions about a possible sale of its insurance business. No terms, proceeds or intended use of proceeds are given.
quotes: DXC acknowledges ongoing discussions regarding a possible sale of its insurance business.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the cited items for revenue and growth; the condition that growth must persist beyond the modification is inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: Insurance Software & Services is the only segment growing: latest-quarter revenue was $394 million, up 23.1% organic, and the six-month figure was $713 million, up 12.4%. The quarter includes a favorable contract modification.
quotes: Organic revenue growth includes a favorable contract modification entered into during the second quarter of fiscal 2027.

growth_thesis.basis: The discussions are stated in the release; the consequence for growth is inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: To keep Insurance as a growth driver, DXC must retain the business and keep bookings above revenue. The evidence shows a possible sale and a book-to-bill of 0.79x.
quotes: DXC acknowledges ongoing discussions regarding a possible sale of its insurance business.

growth_thesis.basis: The expectation is stated by the CEO and in the 10-K; the conditions for it to continue are drawn from the 10-K risk factor on AI.
growth_thesis.claim: Management positions agentic and AI-based solutions as the expected future growth driver, but the evidence does not quantify their revenue.
quotes: making progress with the agentic and AI-based solutions that we expect will contribute to future growth

growth_thesis.basis: Guidance and bookings are stated in the items; the condition that bookings must exceed revenue is inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: Revenue growth requires first stopping the decline. Organic revenue fell 4.0% in the latest quarter, and guidance points to further organic declines of about (6.0)% for the third quarter and (5.5)% to (5.0)% for the full year.
quotes: While our core revenue recovery will take time

growth_thesis.basis: Figures are stated in the 10-Q MD&A; the weight of GIS in the total is from the printed segment percentages.
growth_thesis.claim: Global Infrastructure Services is the largest drag, so any overall growth requires it to stabilize. Its latest-quarter revenue was $1,427 million, down 10.0% organic, and segment profit fell 45.9%.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the cited items; the condition that cuts must outpace the revenue decline is inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: Cost reduction supports profit, though adjusted EBIT still fell. Selling, general and administrative expense was $319 million, down 12.8%, while adjusted EBIT was $187 million, down 26.4%.
quotes: The decline in both periods was primarily driven by lower payroll and related employee benefit costs, as well as reduced professional services and contractor related expenses.

growth_thesis.basis: Share counts and cash flows are stated in the statements; the condition of continued cash generation is inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: Per-share results are helped by buybacks: DXC repurchased $60 million of shares in the latest quarter and $132 million in six months. Diluted weighted shares were 161.99 (table in millions) against 179.15.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the cited items; the sustainability condition is inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: Free cash flow of $405 million for the first half was above the prior year's $337 million, but it includes a one-time $214 million TCS litigation proceed and a $122 million tax deposit outflow. Continued cash generation requires an underlying operating base that does not depend on those items.
quotes: Free cash flow in fiscal 2027 includes cash proceeds of $214 million related to the litigation judgment obtained against TCS

material_events.claim: The President of Global Infrastructure Services resigned, and Paul J. Taylor was appointed President, DXC.
quotes: On July 25, 2026, Mr. Chris Drumgoole notified DXC Technology Company (the “Company”) of his decision to resign as President, Global Infrastructure Services, effective July 30, 2026.

material_events.claim: DXC recognized a litigation judgment against TCS. The gain was $168 million in other income, and cash proceeds were $214 million.
quotes: The increase was primarily due to the $168 million litigation judgment against TCS recognized in the first quarter, partially offset by a $17 million unfavorable change in gains and losses on real estate and facility sales.

material_events.claim: DXC recorded a one-time impairment of transition and transformation costs tied to a customer contract modification, with a related one-time acceleration of software amortization. The amount of the impairment is not stated.
quotes: partially offset by a one-time impairment of transition and transformation costs related to a customer contract modification in the second quarter of fiscal 2027

material_events.claim: Management approved global cost savings initiatives in fiscal 2027, and restructuring costs of $49 million were recorded in the first six months.
quotes: During fiscal 2027, management approved global cost savings initiatives designed to better align our workforce, facility and data center requirements.

material_events.claim: The U.S. Tax Court granted the IRS summary judgment on the foreign currency loss issue, with approximately $125 million of cash tax sought. A final decision on liability is pending, and the 10-K says the expected net liability was fully reserved.
quotes: In March 2026, the Court granted the IRS’ motion for summary judgment.

risks.basis: stated in the cited 10-Q MD&A and earnings release (figures); the mechanism is inferred.
risks.claim: Demand is shrinking. Q2 organic revenue fell 4.0%, Global Infrastructure Services organic revenue fell 10.0%, and Q2 book-to-bill was 0.80x against 0.85x a year earlier.
quotes: Bookings of $2.4 billion declined 10% year-over-year, with a book to bill ratio of 0.80x.

risks.basis: stated in the cited 10-Q MD&A and earnings release; the cost-base mechanism is inferred.
risks.claim: Profitability is eroding faster than revenue. Q2 gross margin fell 280 basis points to 21.8%, adjusted EBIT fell 26.4%, and Global Infrastructure Services segment profit fell 45.9%.
quotes: Gross margin was 21.8% and 21.1% for the second quarter and first six months of fiscal 2027, respectively, a decrease of 280 basis points and 340 basis points against the comparative periods.

risks.basis: stated in the 10-K MD&A (exposure and timing) and the 10-Q MD&A (deposits); the mechanism is inferred.
risks.claim: Unresolved IRS disputes in U.S. Tax Court carry about $655 million of total cash tax exposure. About $523 million of incremental tax expense is unreserved if the company loses the first two issues. The company has already made $122 million of tax deposits with the IRS.
quotes: The total cash tax exposure across all three issues above is approximately $655 million.

risks.basis: stated in the balance sheet, cash flow statement and earnings release; the refinancing mechanism is inferred.
risks.claim: Debt due within a year rose while cash generation weakened. Short-term debt and current maturities were 935 (table in millions) against 520 at March 31, 2026, versus cash of 1,599 (table in millions). Q2 free cash flow was $91 million against $240 million a year earlier.
quotes: Free cash flow(4) was $91 million, compared to $240 million in the second quarter of fiscal year 2026.

risks.basis: stated in the 10-K risk factors; whether it is already happening is not shown.
risks.claim: The company's own risk factors say AI adoption by clients and competitors could substitute for its traditional services and reduce revenue.
quotes: In addition, the rapid adoption of AI technologies by our clients and competitors may reduce demand for certain of our traditional services.

risks.basis: the discussions are stated in the earnings release; the effect on the mix is inferred.
risks.claim: DXC says it is in ongoing discussions about a possible sale of its insurance business, which was the only segment growing in Q2, with organic revenue up 23.1% and segment profit of $45 million.
quotes: DXC acknowledges ongoing discussions regarding a possible sale of its insurance business.

risks.basis: the appointment and resignation are stated in the 8-K; the execution-risk mechanism is stated generally in the 10-K risk factors.
risks.claim: Senior leadership is changing in the weakest segment. The President of Global Infrastructure Services resigned and a new President, DXC was appointed.
quotes: Mr. Drumgoole’s decision to resign was not the result of any disagreement with the Company on any matter relating to the Company's operations, policies or practices.

Any significant leadership change and accompanying senior management transition involves inherent risk and any failure to ensure a smooth transition could hinder our strategic planning, execution and future performance.

unresolved_questions.basis: stated in the cited items (the acknowledgement and the contract-modification note); the segment-mix effect is inferred
unresolved_questions.claim: Will DXC sell its insurance business, and on what terms? The earnings release only acknowledges 'ongoing discussions', and Insurance revenue grew 23.1% organically in Q2, helped by a contract modification.
quotes: DXC acknowledges ongoing discussions regarding a possible sale of its insurance business.
Organic revenue growth includes a favorable contract modification entered into during the second quarter of fiscal 2027.

unresolved_questions.basis: stated in the 10-K MD&A taxes discussion; whether the exposure has changed since 31 March 2026 is not shown in the cited 10-Q passages
unresolved_questions.claim: How will the pending U.S. Tax Court rulings come out, and what cash tax and expense follow? The 10-K says the first and second issues are not fully reserved, with about $523 million of incremental expense if DXC loses and about $655 million of total cash exposure.
quotes: A decision from the court is now pending.

unresolved_questions.basis: stated figures from the release and 10-Q; the link from bookings to future revenue is inferred
unresolved_questions.claim: When will organic revenue stop falling? Q2 bookings were weak (book-to-bill 0.80x), Global Infrastructure organic revenue fell 10.0%, and Q3 guidance is for about a 6.0% organic decline. The CEO says core revenue recovery 'will take time'.
quotes: While our core revenue recovery will take time

unresolved_questions.basis: stated that the items are one-time; their size and the underlying margin are not given in the cited excerpts
unresolved_questions.claim: How much of the 280 basis point gross margin drop to 21.8% in Q2 came from a one-time customer contract modification, and how much from underlying pricing or mix? The size of the one-time impairment and acceleration charges is not in the excerpts.
quotes: Gross margin was 21.8% and 21.1% for the second quarter and first six months of fiscal 2027, respectively, a decrease of 280 basis points and 340 basis points against the comparative periods.

unresolved_questions.basis: balance sheet and cash flow figures are stated; the repayment plan and maturity schedule are not in the cited items
unresolved_questions.claim: How will DXC repay or refinance the larger current debt balance? Short-term debt and current maturities were 935 (table in millions) against 520 at March 2026. DXC repaid 400 of long-term debt and bought back 132 of stock in the half.

unresolved_questions.basis: stated that the resignation and appointment occurred; the new role's remit and the segment succession are not stated in the excerpt
unresolved_questions.claim: Who now leads Global Infrastructure Services, and what is the scope of the new President, DXC role held by Paul Taylor? Global Infrastructure Services is the largest segment, with organic revenue down 10.0% in Q2.
quotes: Resignation of President, Global Infrastructure Services
